tour.name: Aqaba Private Red Sea Day: Snorkelling the Coral Reefs, a Glass-Bottom Boat & Old Aqaba
tour.subtitle: A private day by the Red Sea with a local guide: a boat to the coral reefs of the Aqaba Marine Park, snorkelling at the Japanese Garden and the Cedar Pride wreck, a glass-bottom view of the reef, lunch of fresh fish, and the Mamluk fort and souk of old Aqaba.

tour.overview:
Aqaba, Jordan's only port, lies at the tip of the Gulf of Aqaba on the Red Sea, whose coral reefs are among the richest and most resilient in the world. The Aqaba Marine Park protects several kilometres of reef close to the shore, with hard and soft corals, hundreds of fish species and wrecks such as the Cedar Pride, sunk deliberately in 1985 to create an artificial reef.

This private day takes you onto the water with a local guide and a boat, with snorkelling, a glass-bottom view and a visit to the old town.

AT A GLANCE
• Duration: about 7 hours
• Start and end: your hotel in Aqaba
• Type: private boat and local guide; vehicle for transfers
• Booking: on request – we confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay only then
• Level: easy

WHAT YOU SEE
• The Japanese Garden reef.
• The Cedar Pride wreck.
• A glass-bottom view.
• Old Aqaba.

WHY THIS WORKS
A private boat lets you snorkel at the best sites at the quietest times, with a guide in the water.

WHO IT SUITS
Families, couples, snorkellers and divers.

WHO MAY PREFER ANOTHER TOUR
Add a day in Wadi Rum, just an hour away.

PRACTICAL INFORMATION
The water is warm much of the year. Introductory dives can be added for non-divers.

days.name: Snorkelling in the Aqaba Marine Park, a glass-bottom view and old Aqaba
days.description:
What to expect: the coral reefs of the Red Sea and the old town, with a local guide, private boat, equipment and lunch.

Your guide collects you at about 9:00 and takes you to the marina, where you board your private boat. At the Japanese Garden, a reef of soft and hard corals, you snorkel among parrotfish, butterflyfish, lionfish and moray eels, and often turtles. Through the glass panels of the boat, those who prefer to stay dry see the reef below. At the Cedar Pride, a 74-metre cargo ship lying on its side, you see corals growing on the hull from the surface.

After a lunch of fresh fish and mezze by the sea, you visit old Aqaba: the Mamluk fort, built in the early 16th century and later held by the Arab Revolt led by Sharif Hussein, where Lawrence of Arabia's story intersects; the Arab Revolt flag; and the spice souk, before returning to your hotel.

SCHEDULE (approximate times)
09:00 – Pick-up.
09:30 – Boat to the Japanese Garden.
10:00 – Snorkelling.
11:30 – Cedar Pride wreck.
13:00 – Fish lunch.
14:30 – Aqaba fort and souk.
16:00 – Back at your hotel.

GOOD TO KNOW
• Use reef-safe sun cream.
• An introductory dive can be added.

INCLUDED: private boat and crew, local guide, snorkelling equipment, lunch, fort entrance, bottled water, hotel pick-up and drop-off.
NOT INCLUDED: dives, drinks, tips.

Overnight: none.
Meals: lunch.

faq.question: How does booking on request work?
faq.answer: You choose a date and the number of travellers and send the request. Nothing is charged. We confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay online only when the tour is confirmed.

faq.question: Do we need to be good swimmers?
faq.answer: Basic swimming ability is enough; life vests are available.

faq.question: Can non-swimmers join?
faq.answer: Yes, they can enjoy the glass-bottom view.

faq.question: Can we dive?
faq.answer: Yes, with a dive centre, including introductory dives.

faq.question: Is it suitable for children?
faq.answer: Yes. Child life vests are provided.

faq.question: Is it suitable for people with limited mobility?
faq.answer: Partly; boarding the boat requires steps.

faq.question: Will we be taken to shops?
faq.answer: No. Visiting the souk is optional.

faq.question: What should we bring?
faq.answer: Swimwear, a towel, a hat and reef-safe sun cream.

faq.question: What is the best time of year?
faq.answer: All year; spring and autumn are ideal.

faq.question: Should we tip?
faq.answer: Tipping is customary in Jordan: guides and drivers appreciate a tip if you were happy with their service, but it is always your choice.

faq.question: What is the cancellation policy?
faq.answer: You can cancel free of charge up to 24 hours before the tour. Until your request is confirmed, nothing is charged at all.
